newsitem.title: TURKEY: Uighurs appeal to Turkish rights group for help.
newsitem.headline: Uighurs appeal to Turkish rights group for help.

text.p: Uighur Moslems from China on Monday met officials of Turkey's parliamentary human rights commission to appeal for help against what they say is their mistreatment by Beijing.
"The years of terror and destruction have reached a climax," Riza Bekin, head of the Turkey-based East Turkestan Foundation, told reporters after meeting the commission's chairman, Demir Berberoglu.

Bekin was referring to ethnic unrest in China's mainly Moslem region of Xinjiang, where Beijing says nine people were killed and 198 injured in rioting on February 5-6. Uighurs put the death toll much higher.

Uighur exile groups presented Berberoglu with a report on what they described as "inhuman" activities against them like public torture, extrajudicial killings by firing squad and forced mass abortions.
The majority Uighurs and most of the other Moslem groups in Xinjiang are of ethnic Turkic stock.
